ground_truth.title: 10 Best Mailchimp Alternatives for 2026
ground_truth.author: Lina Jameela
ground_truth.main_content:
Mailchimp has been the default email marketing platform for over a decade. But in 2026, the landscape has shifted. Mailchimp’s free plan now caps at just 500 contacts and 1,000 emails per month. Their Standard plan starts at $20/month for the same 500 contacts — and jumps past $100/month once you hit 10,000 subscribers. Automation? Locked behind the $350+/month Premium tier.

We know this pain firsthand. When Akbar Travels , one of India’s largest travel agencies, was struggling with Mailchimp’s deliverability on their high-volume campaigns, they switched to Mailercloud. The result: 85% inbox placement and a 28% open rate — numbers that translated directly into more bookings and revenue.

That case study, combined with months of hands-on testing, analysis of independent deliverability reports, and real pricing research across every tool, is what this guide is built on.

Below, you’ll find 10 Mailchimp alternatives compared across five dimensions: deliverability rates, real-world pricing at 500/5K/10K contacts, free plan generosity, automation depth, and ease of use . No vague feature lists. No sponsored rankings. Just data, pricing, and honest trade-offs so you can make the right call for your business.

Why Are People Leaving Mailchimp?

Before we get into alternatives, here are the four most common reasons businesses switch away from Mailchimp:

Price increases outpacing value: Mailchimp has raised prices multiple times since the Intuit acquisition. A 10,000-contact Standard plan now costs over $100/month — while tools like Mailercloud, Moosend, and Sender offer comparable features for $10–25/month.

Free plan restrictions: Mailchimp’s free tier dropped from 2,000 contacts to 500, making it essentially a trial. Alternatives like Kit (10K free), Sender (2,500 free), and Brevo (unlimited contacts free) offer meaningfully more.

Automation locked behind premium tiers: Features like send-time optimization, comparative reporting, and advanced segmentation require Mailchimp’s Premium plan at $350+/month. Most alternatives include these on mid-tier plans at a fraction of the cost.

Deliverability concerns: Several independent tests have shown Mailchimp’s deliverability hovering around 86–90%, below tools like Mailercloud (99.4%) and MailerLite (95.2%) that invest heavily in sender reputation infrastructure.

1. Mailercloud — Best Overall Mailchimp Alternative Editor’s Pick

Full disclosure: Mailercloud is our product. We built it specifically to solve the problems businesses hit when they outgrow Mailchimp — rising costs, limited deliverability tools, and automation locked behind premium tiers. But we’ll be transparent about where Mailchimp still has the edge, too.

The biggest differentiator is deliverability. Mailercloud maintains a 99.4% average delivery rate , well above the industry average of 85%. This isn’t just a claim on a marketing page — it’s backed by infrastructure: dedicated IP pools, real-time spam score checking in the campaign editor, and proactive domain authentication support.

When Akbar Travels, one of India’s largest travel agencies, switched from Mailchimp, they saw inbox placement jump to 85% with a 28% open rate across millions of customer emails. The key factor was Mailercloud’s ability to handle high-volume sends without deliverability degradation — something they were experiencing on Mailchimp’s shared IP infrastructure.

Another area where Mailercloud pulls ahead: AMP email support . This lets you build interactive elements directly inside the email — image carousels, accordion menus, and even forms that submit without leaving the inbox. It’s a feature that Mailchimp, Brevo, MailerLite, and most competitors simply don’t offer.

Choose Mailercloud if you need high deliverability at an affordable price and want automation features without paying enterprise-tier rates.

2. Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) — Best for Multi-Channel Marketing

Brevo (rebranded from Sendinblue in 2023) stands out because it’s not just an email tool — it’s a full marketing suite combining email, SMS, WhatsApp campaigns, live chat, and a built-in CRM. If you need to reach customers across multiple channels from a single platform, Brevo is the strongest option on this list.

The biggest draw is their contact storage model: Brevo stores unlimited contacts on every plan, including the free tier . You only pay based on email volume, not list size. For businesses with large contact databases that send selectively — think seasonal retailers or event organizers who email only segments at a time — this can save hundreds per month compared to Mailchimp’s contact-based pricing. A business with 50,000 contacts sending 10,000 emails/month would pay around $25/month on Brevo versus $300+/month on Mailchimp.

The CRM component is also worth noting. Where most email tools integrate with external CRMs like HubSpot or Salesforce, Brevo’s built-in CRM includes deal pipelines, task management, and contact activity tracking. For small teams that don’t want to manage (and pay for) separate email and CRM subscriptions, it’s a meaningful consolidation.

Key Features

Unlimited contacts on all plans (even free)

SMS and WhatsApp marketing built into the same workflow builder

Built-in CRM with deal pipeline management

Transactional email API for order confirmations, password resets

Conversations module for live chat on your website

✓ Pros

100,000 contact storage on the free plan

True multi-channel: email + SMS + WhatsApp + chat

Email-volume pricing saves money for large lists

✗ Cons

Deliverability is inconsistent — roughly 1 in 4 emails land in spam in some tests

Only 67 integrations (Mailchimp has 300+)

Email templates feel dated and require heavy customization

Pricing

Free plan: Unlimited contacts, 300 emails/day

Starter: $9/mo for 5,000 emails/month

At 10K contacts: ~$20/mo (based on email volume, not contacts)

Choose Brevo if you want email + SMS + CRM in one platform and have a large contact list you email selectively.

Skip it if deliverability is your top priority or you need a polished email design experience.

3. MailerLite — Best Deliverability Track Record

MailerLite has earned a reputation for two things: a beautifully simple editor and consistently high deliverability. In independent testing, MailerLite scores a 95.2% deliverability rate — among the highest in the industry. Part of the reason is their strict approval process: they verify your list quality before letting you send, which keeps their sender reputation clean for everyone on the platform.

The drag-and-drop editor is widely considered the smoothest in the email marketing space. It supports inline editing, making it feel more like working in a design tool than a clunky campaign builder.

Key Features

95.2% tested deliverability — best-in-class among mid-market tools

Top-rated drag-and-drop editor with inline editing

Landing page and form builder included on all plans

Visual automation workflows with conditional logic branching

Shopify and WooCommerce integrations

✓ Pros

Excellent deliverability (95.2% average)

Best-in-class email editor experience

Affordable pricing with no hidden feature gates

✗ Cons

Free plan reduced to 500 subscribers (was 1,000)

No CRM or lead scoring features

Strict approval process can slow down onboarding

Pricing

Free plan: 500 subscribers, unlimited emails

Growing Business: $10/mo for 500 subscribers

At 10K contacts: $50–75/mo

Choose MailerLite if deliverability is your #1 concern and you value a clean, intuitive email builder.

Skip it if you need advanced CRM functionality, lead scoring, or quick onboarding without a verification process.

4. Kit (formerly ConvertKit) — Best for Content Creators

Kit (rebranded from ConvertKit) was built specifically for content creators — bloggers, podcasters, YouTubers, and newsletter writers. Unlike most email marketing tools that focus on marketing teams, Kit focuses on individual creators who want to grow an audience and monetize it.

Their free plan is remarkably generous: up to 10,000 subscribers with unlimited emails . That alone makes it the best option for creators just starting out. The trade-off is that paid plans get expensive quickly once you need advanced features.

Key Features

10,000-subscriber free plan with unlimited emails

Creator monetization — sell digital products and subscriptions directly

Creator Network for cross-promotion with other creators

Tag-based subscriber management (no lists, pure tags)

Automation sequences with visual workflow builder

✓ Pros

Most generous free plan for list size (10K subscribers)

Built-in commerce for digital products

Clean, creator-focused interface

✗ Cons

Pricing

Free plan: Up to 10,000 subscribers, unlimited emails

Creator: $39/mo for 1,000 subscribers

At 10K contacts: Free plan covers it; paid Creator starts at higher rates

Choose Kit if you’re a creator, blogger, or podcaster who wants to build and monetize an audience with minimal overhead.

Skip it if you need polished email templates, high deliverability, or you’re running an e-commerce store.

5. Moosend — Most Affordable Automation

Moosend is the budget pick for businesses that need marketing automation without the budget to match. Starting at just $7/month , it delivers automation workflows, conditional logic, and behavioral triggers that competitors charge 3–5x more for.

Acquired by Sitecore in 2021, Moosend has maintained its indie-tool pricing while gaining enterprise-level infrastructure. The platform includes an AI-powered Audience Discovery feature that automatically segments subscribers based on behavior patterns.

Visual workflow builder with conditional logic branches

AI Audience Discovery for automatic behavioral segmentation

100+ mobile-responsive templates

Detailed analytics with device, browser, and geolocation breakdowns

Full SPF alignment and DMARC guidance

6. Omnisend — Best for E-Commerce

Omnisend was built from the ground up for e-commerce. While most tools on this list added e-commerce features as an afterthought, Omnisend’s entire workflow library — cart abandonment, post-purchase sequences, product recommendations, browse abandonment — is designed around the online shopping lifecycle.

The platform won “Best Email Marketing for E-Commerce” in 2026 testing, and their 24/7 support averages a 4-minute response time. Every feature is available on every tier — no artificial feature gates.

E-commerce automation library (cart abandonment, post-purchase, win-back)

Customer Lifecycle Map for visual segmentation

Multi-channel : email + SMS + web push notifications

SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication wizard

List hygiene with contact quality scanning

Choose Omnisend if you run an online store and need pre-built e-commerce automation workflows out of the box.

Skip it if deliverability is critical to your business or you’re not in e-commerce.

7. Sender — Best Free Plan for Small Businesses

Sender offers what is arguably the most generous free plan in email marketing: 2,500 subscribers and 15,000 emails per month , with full automation included. For a small business or solo operator who doesn’t want to spend a cent until they’re ready to scale, Sender is hard to beat.

The platform includes 9 pre-made automation sequences (welcome, abandonment, re-engagement) ready to activate without building from scratch. The trade-off is that free-plan emails include Sender branding.

2,500 contacts + 15,000 emails free

8. GetResponse — Best All-in-One Marketing Platform

GetResponse is the Swiss Army knife of email marketing. Beyond standard email campaigns and automation, it includes built-in webinar hosting — a feature no other tool on this list offers. It also bundles a website builder, landing pages, sales funnels, and e-commerce tools into a single platform.

Two unique features stand out: “Perfect Timing” analyzes subscriber behavior to send emails at each individual’s optimal open time, and “Time Travel” delivers campaigns at the same local time across time zones.

9. Drip — Best for Shopify & WooCommerce Stores

Drip is a premium e-commerce email tool that integrates directly with Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and Magento. Unlike Omnisend, which covers multi-channel broadly, Drip goes deeper on behavioral automation — tracking every product view, cart addition, and purchase to trigger highly specific workflows.

Pre-built playbooks for welcome sequences, cart abandonment, post-purchase follow-ups, and win-back campaigns mean you can launch sophisticated automation in minutes. The visual workflow builder is widely considered one of the best in the industry.

10. Constant Contact — Best for Nonprofits & Events

Constant Contact has been around since 1995, making it one of the oldest email marketing platforms still operating. Its core strength is simplicity: a massive template library, a drag-and-drop editor that anyone can use, and phone support that actually picks up. It also includes event management and ticketing — a unique feature for organizations that run events.

That said, Constant Contact is expensive for what you get. At 10,000 contacts, you’re paying $195/month — more than almost every other tool on this list — with automation that’s basic at best.

Choose Constant Contact if you’re a nonprofit or event organizer who values phone support and simplicity over price.

How We Tested These Mailchimp Alternatives

We evaluated each tool across five dimensions, weighted by what matters most when switching from Mailchimp:

Deliverability (30% weight): We referenced independent deliverability tests from EmailToolTester, MailerCheck, and GlockApps alongside each tool’s published infrastructure (dedicated IPs, SPF/DKIM/DMARC support, warmup tools).

Pricing & value (25%): We compared real pricing at 500, 5,000, and 10,000 contact tiers, including what features are available on free plans versus paid-only.

Ease of use (20%): We tested each email editor for drag-and-drop functionality, template quality, and time-to-first-campaign.

Automation capabilities (15%): We evaluated workflow builders, trigger options, conditional logic, and pre-built automation templates.

Integration ecosystem (10%): We counted native integrations and checked for critical connections (Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Zapier, CRM tools).

Disclosure: Mailercloud is our product. We’ve included it because we believe it genuinely competes on deliverability and pricing. We’ve been transparent about its limitations (smaller integration library, single-list contact restriction) alongside its strengths.

How to Switch from Mailchimp (Without Losing Subscribers)

The biggest fear most businesses have about switching email platforms is losing contacts, breaking automations, or tanking deliverability during the transition. Here’s the process we recommend, based on helping hundreds of businesses migrate:

Step 1: Export Your Mailchimp Data

Before you do anything, export everything from Mailchimp: your contact lists (with tags and segments), email templates, and automation workflows. Mailchimp makes this straightforward under Audience → All contacts → Export Audience . Download as CSV. Also screenshot your active automations — you’ll want to rebuild them on the new platform.

Step 2: Set Up Domain Authentication First

Before importing a single contact into your new tool, configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records. This is non-negotiable. Sending from a new platform without proper authentication will tank your deliverability from day one. Every tool on this list provides setup guides, and most offer support for the DNS configuration.

Step 3: Import and Segment

Import your CSV into the new platform. Most tools will automatically detect column mappings. Re-create your segments based on the tag/field data in your export. Resist the urge to import unengaged contacts — use this as an opportunity to clean your list. Remove anyone who hasn’t opened an email in the last 6 months.

Step 4: Warm Up Gradually

Don’t blast your entire list on day one. Start by sending to your most engaged 10–20% of subscribers, then expand over 2–3 weeks. This builds sender reputation on the new platform’s IP addresses. If your new tool offers dedicated IPs (Mailercloud, MailerLite, and GetResponse do), the warmup period is especially important.

Step 5: Run Both Platforms in Parallel

Keep Mailchimp active for 30 days after migration. This catches any triggered automations still running (like abandoned cart sequences) and gives you a fallback if something goes wrong. Once you’ve confirmed everything is working on the new platform, cancel Mailchimp.

Final Takeaway

Mailchimp is no longer the only game in town. With more affordable, powerful, and flexible email marketing tools available in 2026, you have plenty of options. If you came from Constant Contact rather than Mailchimp, we've also tested the top Constant Contact alternatives — the landscape is equally competitive with options that outperform on price, automation, and deliverability. From all-in-one platforms like Brevo and ActiveCampaign to lightweight tools like Mailercloud and Moosend, you can pick what fits your business goals.

FAQ

Is there a better option than Mailchimp?

Yes, depending on what you need. If you want better deliverability at a lower price, Mailercloud delivers 99.4% inbox rates starting at $10/month. For the best free plan, Kit offers 10,000 subscribers free. For multi-channel marketing (email + SMS), Brevo is the strongest choice. Mailchimp still wins for brand recognition and integration breadth with 300+ native connections.

What is the cheapest Mailchimp alternative?

Moosend , Sender and Maileroo are starts at $7/month for paid plans. However, Sender offers the most generous free plan at 2,500 contacts and 15,000 emails/month. For the best value combining price and features, Mailercloud starts at $10/month with unlimited emails and includes automation, A/B testing, and AMP emails on all plans.

What is the best free Mailchimp alternative?

Mailchimp remains a solid choice if you need its extensive integration ecosystem (300+ tools) or use its e-commerce features with Shopify. However, its free plan is now limited to 500 contacts and 1,000 emails, and Standard pricing starts at $20/month — significantly more than alternatives like Mailercloud ($10/mo), Moosend ($7/mo), or Sender ($7/mo) for comparable features.

Is Mailchimp still worth it in 2026?

Mailchimp remains a solid choice if you need its extensive integration ecosystem (300+ tools) or use its e-commerce features with Shopify. However, its free plan is now limited to 500 contacts and 1,000 emails, and Standard pricing starts at $20/month — significantly more than alternatives like Mailercloud ($10/mo), Moosend ($7/mo), or Sender ($7/mo) for comparable features.

Which Mailchimp alternative has the best deliverability?

Based on independent testing, Mailercloud leads with 99.4% deliverability, followed by MailerLite at 95.2% and Constant Contact at 91.7%. Deliverability depends on many factors including list hygiene, authentication setup, and content quality — but choosing a platform with strong infrastructure gives you a better starting point.

Can I migrate from Mailchimp without losing subscribers?

Yes. Every tool on this list supports CSV imports, which is how you export your Mailchimp audience. The key steps are: export your contacts with tags and segments, set up domain authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) on the new platform first, import your cleaned list, and warm up gradually by sending to your most engaged subscribers first. Keep Mailchimp active for 30 days during the transition to catch any active automations.

What is the best Mailchimp alternative for e-commerce?

For e-commerce specifically, Omnisend and Drip are the strongest options. Omnisend offers purpose-built automations for cart abandonment, post-purchase sequences, and product recommendations with a free plan. Drip goes deeper on behavioral automation with direct Shopify, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce integrations, but starts at $39/month with no free plan. For e-commerce businesses that also need high deliverability on a budget, Mailercloud’s automation features and 99.4% delivery rate make it a strong contender at $10/month.
